label: 10x Genomics HDF5
definition: HDF5 file format produced by 10x Genomics Cell Ranger (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 or raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5) storing a sparse cell-by-feature count matrix together with barcodes and feature metadata for single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, or Multiome experiments.

label: AnnData Zarr
definition: Zarr-based on-disk representation of the AnnData object following the AnnData 0.9+ zarr specification, enabling out-of-core and distributed access to single-cell count matrices and metadata. Used by TileDB-SOMA, CellxGene, and the new anndata API for cloud-native single-cell data stores.

label: Apache Parquet
definition: Apache Parquet is an open-source columnar storage file format for efficient analytical queries on large tabular datasets, supporting nested data structures, dictionary encoding, and column-level compression. Widely used in bioinformatics cloud pipelines for storing GWAS summary statistics, single-cell metadata, and population-scale phenotype tables.

label: Arrow IPC
definition: Apache Arrow Inter-Process Communication (IPC) format, including the Feather v2 on-disk layout, for storing typed tabular data in a columnar memory-mapped layout enabling zero-copy reads. Used in bioinformatics for high-throughput data exchange between Python, R, and Rust-based tools.

label: BEDPE
definition: Paired-end BED format for representing structural variants or chromatin interactions as pairs of genomic intervals, with each record encoding two chromosomal loci (chrom1, start1, end1, chrom2, start2, end2) plus optional name, score, and strand columns. Used by LUMPY, Manta, and bedtools pairtopair.

label: BGEN
definition: Binary format for storing imputed or genotyped variants with probabilistic genotype dosages and uncertainty, developed for the UK Biobank and used by tools such as BOLT-LMM, REGENIE, and SAIGE for large-scale association analysis.

label: BLOW5
definition: The binary (blocked, compressed) version of SLOW5 for Oxford Nanopore raw signal data, providing random access and smaller file sizes than SLOW5 while retaining the same record semantics. Converted from SLOW5 using slow5tools.

label: Cooler
definition: HDF5-based format for storing Hi-C and other chromosome conformation capture contact matrices at one or multiple resolutions, used by the Cooler library. Multi-resolution cooler files (.mcool) contain matrices at a geometric series of bin sizes enabling zoom-level access in genome browsers such as HiGlass.

label: FAST5
definition: HDF5-based binary format produced by Oxford Nanopore sequencers for storing raw electrical signal (squiggles) and basecalled nucleotide sequences, with associated read metadata. The legacy ONT format, superseded by POD5 for raw signal storage.

label: FCS
definition: Flow Cytometry Standard binary format for storing per-event fluorescence intensity measurements across multiple detector channels from flow cytometry or mass cytometry (CyTOF) experiments, as specified by the ISAC FCS standard (versions 2.0, 3.0, 3.1).

label: Fragments file
definition: Tab-separated text file (typically BGZF-compressed with Tabix index) produced by 10x Genomics Cell Ranger ATAC or ArchR preprocessing, listing per-cell chromatin accessibility fragments as chromosome, start, end, cell barcode, and read count. Standard input for scATAC-seq peak-calling and per-cell accessibility matrix construction.

label: GWAS-SSF
definition: GWAS Summary Statistics Format (SSF) defined by GWAS Catalog and Open GWAS: a standardized tab-separated text format for sharing genome-wide association study summary statistics, including required columns for variant ID, chromosome, position, effect/other alleles, beta/OR, standard error, p-value, and allele frequency.

label: H5AD
definition: HDF5-backed file format for the AnnData object (Python anndata library), storing a cell-by-feature matrix together with cell and feature metadata, unstructured annotations, dimensionality reduction embeddings, and neighborhood graphs. The primary on-disk format for Scanpy-based single-cell analysis workflows.

label: .hic
definition: Binary format produced by the Juicer pipeline and readable by Juicebox for storing genome-wide chromatin contact matrices from Hi-C experiments at multiple resolutions, including expected interaction counts and normalization vectors.

label: MEX
definition: Market Exchange Format: a three-file bundle (matrix.mtx.gz, barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz) produced by 10x Genomics Cell Ranger, STARsolo, Alevin-fry, or kallisto bustools to represent a sparse cell-by-feature count matrix for single-cell sequencing experiments.

label: Modkit pileup
definition: Tab-separated text format produced by ONT Modkit (and compatible with bedMethyl) for reporting per-position base modification frequencies from aligned nanopore reads, storing chromosome, position, strand, modification code (e.g., m, h), valid coverage, fraction modified, and count columns.

label: NIfTI
definition: Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative format for storing brain MRI, fMRI, and other volumetric medical image data in a single .nii or dual .hdr/.img file, carrying voxel intensities together with spatial orientation metadata. Supports both uncompressed (.nii) and gzip-compressed (.nii.gz) variants.

label: ONNX
definition: Open Neural Network Exchange format: an open standard for representing machine learning model architectures and trained weights, enabling interoperability between frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX) and deployment runtimes. Used in bioinformatics for distributing protein structure prediction, variant effect, and sequence embedding models.

label: Pairs
definition: Tab-separated text format defined by the 4D Nucleome (4DN) consortium for recording read-pair alignments from Hi-C and related chromatin conformation capture experiments, storing chromosome, position, and strand for each side of a ligation junction together with pair-type classification.

label: PLINK binary
definition: Binary genotype format used by the PLINK 1.9 and PLINK 2 toolsets, comprising three files: .bed (compact binary genotype calls), .bim (variant annotation), and .fam (sample pedigree and phenotype), used for large-scale genome-wide association studies and population genetics.

label: POD5
definition: Oxford Nanopore Technologies' current binary format for raw electrical signal data, replacing FAST5. Uses Apache Arrow IPC internally and supports efficient random access, signal compression, and per-read metadata storage, as written by MinKNOW and consumed by Dorado.

label: PyTorch model
definition: PyTorch serialized model format (.pt or .pth) storing model weights via Python pickle or the more portable TorchScript export, used to distribute trained deep learning models for sequence analysis, structure prediction, and single-cell foundation model fine-tuning.

label: SafeTensors
definition: Hugging Face SafeTensors format for storing neural network weight tensors: a simple, safe binary format that does not execute arbitrary code on load, supports memory mapping for zero-copy access, and is the preferred distribution format for large bioinformatics foundation models such as ESM-2, Nucleotide Transformer, and scGPT.

label: SLOW5
definition: A text-based (ASCII) format for Oxford Nanopore raw signal data that is an interoperability alternative to FAST5/POD5, designed for streaming and pipeline integration. Each record stores signal data and read metadata in a simple tab-delimited layout.

label: Spectral library
definition: A reference database of experimentally acquired or predicted MS/MS fragment ion spectra - including precursor m/z, charge, retention time, and peptide sequence - stored in formats such as BLIB (BiblioSpec), DLIB (EncyclopeDIA), or TSV/CSV, used by DIA-MS tools such as Spectronaut, DIA-NN, and OpenSWATH for targeted peptide quantification.

label: Visium spatial format
definition: 10x Genomics Visium output format consisting of a gene expression count matrix (MEX or HDF5) paired with a tissue_positions_list.csv (or parquet) file mapping spot barcodes to pixel and array coordinates, plus a high-resolution tissue image, as produced by Space Ranger for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
